reader.requirement: At --std 85, the RECORD KEY names the prime key and no two records of the file may hold the same prime key value: a WRITE that would duplicate it fails (22 in random/dynamic access, 21 when a sequential-access WRITE is not ascending), equality being judged in the native collating sequence (§1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3) whatever the program collating sequence.

edition-consulted.switches: the connector's Edition only; prime uniqueness in IndexedConnector#Write tests no edition
nothing by edition: no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause means native order at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|DialectBehaviors|Edition in IndexedConnector.cs (only ReadRandom and SelectSequentialRecord consult it, neither on the WRITE path) and in FileControlBinder.cs#ResolveFileCollating
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f16_05 covers a dynamic-access duplicate WRITE (22); not covered: sequential access (21), OPEN I-O random access, REWRITE of a missing key, a group key with numeric subordinates, and the program collating sequence

probes.printed: W1 00; W2 IK 21 (sequential, equal key); W3 00; W4 00 (C000 after B001); W5 IK 22 (random, I-O); W6 00; R1 00 B001TWO; RW 00; RW2 IK 23; SEQ A001ONE, B001NEW, C000THR, C001FOUR; END 10
probes.expected: §1985:IX.1.3.4: 21 for a sequential ascending violation, 22 for a duplicate prime key, 23 for a REWRITE of a missing record; with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE 'A' ALSO 'B' ALSO 'C', native order still keys the file (§1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3)

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.2.7.4 GR1  (2.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:IX.1.3.4  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.3a
OK  §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3  (2.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: IndexedConnector#Write looks the prime key up before releasing and answers 22, after a sequential-access ascending check that answers 21. An ALSO alphabet as program collating sequence does not make distinct keys collide, as §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3 requires.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-092/pku-001 (src/pku.cob): byte-exact uniqueness against normalizing comparisons and OPEN EXTEND (not in the reader's probes). Printed: W1 00 'AB  ', W2 00 'AB'+LOW-VALUE x2, W3 00 'AB'+HIGH-VALUE x2, W4 00 'ab  ', W5 IK 22 (repeat 'AB  '), W6 00 'ZZZZ'; OPEN EXTEND through a second sequential-access FD on the same file: OX 00, X1 IK 21 ('ZZZZ' below the highest key 'ab  '), X2 IK 21, X3 IK 21, X4 IK 21; the read-back R01..R05 is LOW2, SPC1, HIG3, ZZZ6, LOWC, END 10 (native ascending order, the failed writes left the file unaffected). Trailing spaces, low-values and high-values are distinct key values; equality is never padded or case-folded. 21 is §1985:IX.1.3.4's sequence error for successive keys not ascending. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.2.7.4 GR1  (2.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:IX.1.3.4  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.3a' (quote 'the ascending sequence requirements for successive record key values are violated').
